findings.finding: The plan names three options for threading the step ID to `usage_log.record()` and instructs the implementer to 'Pick ONE and record why,' implicitly endorsing the ContextVar route via the `_active_gate_config` precedent. However, the plan specifies no RETIRE/reset path for the ContextVar after each step completes, particularly in error paths. If steps execute sequentially within the same asyncio Task (rather than as separate Tasks, which would auto-scope the ContextVar), a step that exits via exception — or any step that simply doesn't clear the var — leaves a stale step ID active for the next step. The plan does not specify whether steps run as separate Tasks or in the same task context, which is the fact that determines whether ContextVar scoping is sufficient or an explicit reset is required.

findings.suggested_fix: For the ContextVar option: require the step executor to capture the reset token at set time (`token = _active_step_id.set(step_id)`) and call `_active_step_id.reset(token)` in a `finally` block, matching the pattern Python's own contextvars documentation recommends for scoped mutation.

AC1 only requires the outcome ('every REBAR_USAGE_LOG record carries the STEP ID'), not the documented decision.
findings.finding: The Approach section describes a deliverable — a documented rationale for the threading mechanism choice ('record why') — that has no corresponding acceptance criterion. An implementation could select a threading option without recording the rationale, and no AC would catch the omission.
findings.location: Approach → STEP 0 → 'THE THREADING PROBLEM'; Acceptance Criteria section
scenarios: Implementer selects option (b) (overloading `target` dict) without documenting why, which the plan explicitly warns against ('overloads a field meaning something else'), and no AC catches this.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the Testing section that the recording runner captures the RESOLVED model string (the value that would be sent to the provider), not the declared class token, and assert against that resolved value.
evidence: 'a fake that captures the model it is handed per step' — 'handed' is ambiguous about whether this is pre- or post-resolution

The defect is that a class token is never passed to the resolver — the fixture must assert on the RESOLVED model string, not the declared token, to distinguish 'declaration honoured' from 'declaration ignored'
findings.finding: The recording-runner fixture described in the Testing section does not specify the capture point: if the fake records the model value it is *handed* rather than the model value *after class resolution*, it can pass the test on today's broken code (the runner receives a class token but resolves it to cfg.model — the fixture would see the unresolved token, not the wrong resolved model).
findings.location: Testing section / 'execute the code-review gate with a recording runner (a fake that captures the model it is handed per step)'
scenarios: A recording runner that intercepts at RunRequest construction (pre-resolution) will always see the raw token and can never distinguish the bug from the fix.
A recording runner that intercepts at the LLM HTTP call (post-resolution) will see the real model string and will correctly catch the bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'a fake that captures the model it is handed per step' with 'a fake that intercepts at the same chokepoint as usage_log.record() (i.e. post-resolution, at the LLM call boundary) and records the resolved model string per step'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test (and a specified behavior) for `usage_log.record()` when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set but no step context is active (ContextVar not set / call made outside a step executor), covering both what is written and that the record remains valid for `summarize()`.
evidence: Plan says 'record() must stay a no-op when REBAR_USAGE_LOG is unset' but is silent on the case where the log IS enabled and no step ContextVar has been set.

The measured 9-call log includes 'code-novelty' at index 9 — a call that does not belong to any of the five declared code-review steps, so no step context would be active for it under the proposed ContextVar design.
AC line 'the addition is ADDITIVE and inert when unconfigured' covers only the REBAR_USAGE_LOG-unset case, not the enabled-but-no-step-context case.
findings.finding: The testing plan does not specify or test the behavior of `usage_log.record()` when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` IS set but no step context is active (e.g., the `code-novelty` call at index 9 in the measured log, which is not attributed to any step in `code-review.yaml`). With a ContextVar-based threading approach (option c, which the plan leans toward), this call would read None from the ContextVar; the plan does not specify whether to emit a null field, omit it, or raise, and no AC or test covers this path.
findings.location: Scope / Step 0 — usage_log.py; Acceptance Criteria (additive/inert AC)
scenarios: ContextVar approach is chosen; code-novelty (or any call outside a step executor) fires; record() writes a record with a missing/null step field; summarize() or downstream consumers break on the unexpected shape.
A test for step attribution passes only for in-step calls; the out-of-step call is never exercised, so a bug where it throws is not caught until a live run.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: when no step context is active, emit `step_id: null` (or omit the field) and ensure summarize() tolerates both shapes. Add one AC line: 'a record written outside a step context (e.g. code-novelty) carries step_id: null and does not break summarize().' Add a unit test for this case alongside the existing no-op-when-unset test.

'every future per-step or per-provider question in this epic (0d76's parity arms, eb6e's cutover, 8625's docs) needs exactly this attribution'

findings.finding: The plan introduces a new JSONL schema for `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` records (adding `step_id` and declared `class` fields) that other named epic stories (0d76, eb6e, 8625) explicitly rely on as a data source, but no update to any schema doc, reference doc, or cross-ticket note is called out — leaving those consumers with stale field descriptions.
findings.location: Scope / STEP 0 — observability; AC bullets 1–3
scenarios: A developer reading the 0d76, eb6e, or 8625 plan/docs sees the old REBAR_USAGE_LOG field list (op, model, provider) and writes parsing code that ignores the new step_id/class fields, defeating the attribution goal.
A future probe written against a stale schema doc omits the step filter, reproducing the exact ambiguity this story was created to eliminate.
findings.suggested_fix: In `usage_log.py`, add a module-level docstring (or a `# SCHEMA:` block comment above `record()`) enumerating all fields: `op`, `model`, `provider`, `step_id` (new), `class` (new, optional).
